public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic burn billions annually, have worsening margins, and have no path to profitability.

statement.excerpt: The most-prominent companies in the AI industry — Anthropic and OpenAI — burn billions of dollars a year, have margins that get worse over time, and absolutely no path to profitability, yet the majority of the media act as if this is a problem that they will fix, even going as far as to make up rationalizations as to how they’ll fix it, focusing on big revenue numbers that wilt under scrutiny.

from_speaker: burn billions of dollars a year
margins that get worse over time
our_interpretation: The normalized financial proposition is assessed; the separate assertion about a majority of media coverage is not included.
Annual burn refers to cash consumption, not accounting net losses or gross spending.
For the ongoing annual assertion, 2025 is the latest completed calendar year before the post. Margin trends require a comparable 2024 baseline.
Margins ordinarily means profit as a share of revenue, but the speaker does not specify gross, operating, net, or adjusted margins.
No path to profitability is read as an assertion about the business economics then available, not as a forecast that the companies can never become profitable.
The supplied financial assertion names no source or accounting basis; the contract basis remains unknown.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records show each company consuming multiple billions of dollars annually, worsening margins on a consistent basis, and no economically substantiated route to profitability under the business conditions described.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records materially contradict annual cash consumption or margin deterioration, or establish an economically substantiated profitability route that defeats the categorical assertion.
